samples.question: The two rows at the top are equalities: the black shapes left of a double bar are worth exactly the circles to its right, and a circle is worth one. Neither row prices a shape on its own, so use both together to find what a triangle and a square are worth. The two gray pans are not worth the same. Exactly one colored purse holds shapes worth exactly the difference between the pans, so adding it to the lighter pan would balance them. Which purse is it? Answer blue, green, orange, or purple.
